    • getResourceGroups

      @GetMapping("/departments/{deptId}/resourcegroups") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<List<ResourceGroupDTO>> getResourceGroups(@PathVariable Long deptId, @AuthenticatedUser PUser currentUser)
      Returns the resource groups of a department. Without this, a REST consumer cannot discover any group id: groups could be created and deleted, but never listed, so the group-scoped reads (/resourcegroups/{groupId}/resources) had no reachable entry point.
      Parameters:
      deptId - ID of the department
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with the department's resource groups

    • getAllResources

      @GetMapping("/resources") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<List<ResourceDTO>> getAllResources(@AuthenticatedUser PUser currentUser)
      Returns every resource the current user may read, across all groups and departments. The flat enumeration entry point for consumers (e.g. a dashboard): the per-group endpoints require group ids that a REST client cannot otherwise discover.
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with the list of readable resources

    • getResourceStatus

      @GetMapping("/resources/status") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<List<ResourceStatusDTO>> getResourceStatus(@AuthenticatedUser PUser currentUser)
      Returns every readable resource together with its latest telemetry readings and its monitoring rules — the same picture as /resources plus /resources/{id}/values/latest plus /resources/{id}/telemetry-rules, but in a single call instead of 1 + 2N. Meant for status views that poll: those paid the fan-out on every tick, and every one of those calls re-authenticated and re-resolved the caller.
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with the status of every readable resource

    • clearCostRate

      @DeleteMapping("/resources/{id}/cost-rate") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<ResourceDTO> clearCostRate(@PathVariable Long id, @AuthenticatedUser PUser currentUser)
      Removes the cost rate, so the resource is no longer charged for.

      Its own endpoint because PATCH cannot express it: there null means "unchanged", which is what makes a partial update partial, so no request body can say "remove this". The three cost fields also only make sense together — clearing them one at a time would go through a state the validation rejects. Both reasons are specific to removal, which is why this is a small endpoint rather than a change to PATCH semantics across the API.

      Parameters:
      id - ID of the resource
      Returns:
      the resource without its cost rate

    • cancelReservation

      @DeleteMapping("/reservations/{reservationId}") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Void> cancelReservation(@PathVariable Integer reservationId, @AuthenticatedUser PUser currentUser)
      Cancels a reservation and releases the occupied slot. Allowed for the owner of the reservation or a user with UPDATE rights on the resource.
      Parameters:

      Returns:
      204 No Content on success

    • sendCommand

      @PostMapping("/resources/{id}/command") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Void> sendCommand(@PathVariable Long id, @RequestBody ResourceController.ResourceCommandRequest request, @AuthenticatedUser PUser currentUser)
      Sends a control command to a resource. The transport (MQTT/REST) is chosen automatically (MQTT preferred when online, otherwise REST fallback). The addressed slot is derived server-side from the user's active reservation — the client supplies no slot.
      Parameters:
      id - ID of the resource
      request - command and optional free parameter
      Returns:
      202 Accepted, if the command was handed off

    • recordValue

      @PostMapping("/resources/{id}/values") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Void> recordValue(@PathVariable Long id, @RequestBody ResourceController.ResourceValueRequest request, @AuthenticatedUser PUser currentUser)
      Records a telemetry reading for a resource (REST ingest). Enables devices without MQTT — and manual/Bruno calls — to report values. The reading is appended to the named data point's history, mirroring the MQTT VALUE path. Requires UPDATE permission on the resource.
      Parameters:
      id - ID of the resource
      request - data point name and value (both mandatory)
      Returns:
      202 Accepted once the reading has been recorded

    • getLatestValues

      @GetMapping("/resources/{id}/values/latest") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<List<ResourceValueDTO>> getLatestValues(@PathVariable Long id, @AuthenticatedUser PUser currentUser)
      Returns the newest reading of every telemetry data point of a resource — the read counterpart to the ingest above. A dashboard renders one value per data point without pulling the full history. Requires READ permission on the resource.
      Parameters:
      id - ID of the resource
      Returns:
      ResponseEntity with the latest value per data point (empty when none recorded)
